articles.title: Breaking: ED Report Sparks Punjab Political Storm, High Court to Hear Corruption Case Today
articles.description: Punjab politics has entered a fresh phase of confrontation after an Enforcement Directorate (ED) report submitted before the Punjab and Haryana High Court raised serious allegations of an alleged corruption network linked to government functioning. The 200-page report, highlighted in ABP News’ Operation Punjab, has triggered a political storm, with the Bhagwant Mann government facing intense opposition scrutiny. The report reportedly names Rajveer Ghuman, described as an Officer on Special Duty to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, along with Nitin Goyal, who is alleged to have acted as an intermediary between officials and Ghuman. The ED investigation reportedly details 21 transfer and posting-related instances and refers to seven cases connected with arms licences. The allegations also reportedly cover transfers and postings, tenders, change-of-land-use permissions for builders and appointments within the Chief Minister’s Office. According to the reported findings, electronic devices and documents recovered during the investigation allegedly provided information about financial transactions and an organised network. The ED had reportedly conducted searches at locations linked to Goyal in May, during which two bags allegedly containing cash were thrown from a balcony. The agency reportedly seized ₹21 lakh from the bags. The matter reached the Punjab and Haryana High Court after the ED allegedly sought responses from the Punjab government and police on multiple occasions. The court is scheduled to hear the case today, making the proceedings politically significant. Meanwhile, the Shiromani Akali Dal is set to meet Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria under Sukhbir Singh Badal’s leadership. The BJP has also demanded Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation and called for an independent investigation. The allegations remain subject to judicial scrutiny and further investigation.

articles.title: Breaking: Kharge Writes to Nadda Over Purification Row, Seeks FIR and Action After 24 Days
articles.description: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has renewed the political battle over the controversial “purification” incident, writing a two-page letter to former BJP president and Union Minister J.P. Nadda. Kharge has questioned the delay in action and sought clarity on the assurance given in Parliament regarding an inquiry into the matter. According to Kharge’s letter, he had raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha on August 13 and demanded immediate action. He now points out that 24 days have passed, but an FIR has allegedly not been registered against the individuals or organisations he holds responsible. Kharge has urged Nadda to ensure that the matter is investigated and appropriate legal action is taken against those found guilty. The Congress has described the incident as a serious issue linked to social discrimination and alleged that the manner in which the “purification” was carried out was objectionable. The controversy has already triggered a political confrontation, with Congress workers staging protests in Uttarakhand and raising the issue beyond the state. The BJP has previously maintained that neither the party nor its members were involved in the incident and had indicated that the matter would be examined and action taken if wrongdoing was established. Kharge has now brought the issue back into the political spotlight by publicly sharing his letter on social media. The development is likely to intensify the war of words between the Congress and BJP, with attention now turning to whether Nadda or the BJP will respond to Kharge’s fresh demand for an FIR and investigation.
